original_definitions.hypothesis: A recent progressive handicap chase winner can be worth opposing where a rise meets specific comparable chase evidence in the opposition; the rise alone is insufficient.
original_definitions.mechanism: Changed effective terms may narrow a demonstrated form margin, while an established rival or claimant supplies a concrete winning route.
original_definitions.scope: All 46 Saturday UK/Irish races screened in this review; final active favourite/joint favourite or close market leader in a handicap chase, latest completed race a chase win, higher handicap burden, and a named rival with comparable demonstrated chase evidence. Fix current eligibility now and record exclusions.
original_definitions.scope_exclusions: Rock My Way did not win his latest race; Realta Liath did not win latest; Chosen Hero’s latest win was a hurdle, not a chase; Steel Ally’s race is not a handicap. Flat and hurdle handicap winners are outside this version.
original_definitions.counterargument: Both qualifiers can improve beyond their raised marks; reappearance form and course suitability can justify favouritism.
original_definitions.limitations: Qualitative entry comparisons; no calibrated probabilities; jockey claims are not guaranteed ability gains; two differently selected groups must be shown separately.
original_definitions.weakening_evidence: Repeated favourite wins despite favourable rival comparisons; failed direct-form reversals; net losses at the actual frozen prices; profit concentrated in few results or one condition.
original_definitions.revision_policy: Retain v1 and prospectively date any changed definition; do not refit past results.

original_definitions.hypothesis: A leading chase debutant may be opposable when multiple rivals have credible useful jumping ability and specific routes to transferring it to fences, while the favourite’s own transfer case remains consequential.
original_definitions.mechanism: Alternative useful jumpers may translate proven hurdle/point ability sufficiently to beat the market-leading recruit; chase inexperience itself is not the mechanism.
original_definitions.scope: All 46 Saturday UK/Irish races screened; active market-leading novice/beginners chase horse with no prior Rules chase start, useful own hurdle/point case, and at least one rival with useful established jumping evidence plus another specific supported route.
original_definitions.scope_exclusions: Koktail Divin and Kiss Will already have chase form; Lulamba is NR and already has chase form; Lastbutnotleased runs over hurdles and Mister Boum in a bumper, outside this theory.
original_definitions.counterargument: Mighty Park may be a much better chaser; opposition also has uncertain transfers.
original_definitions.limitations: Only one present candidate; no causal proof or calibrated probability; do not interpret every chase debut defeat as validation.
original_definitions.weakening_evidence: Favourite’s superior jumping/class decides the race, rivals fail to transfer or none of the named rivals supplies the anticipated mechanism; negative price-based P/L.
original_definitions.revision_policy: Version changes prospectively; keep old outcomes and definitions.

original_definitions.hypothesis: In maiden hurdles, demonstrated useful hurdle competition may be sufficient to oppose a market-leading bumper winner on hurdling debut at an independently accepted Lay quote.
original_definitions.mechanism: Prior hurdle performance may translate to a more reliable winning route than the favourite’s still-unproven hurdle transfer, while the favourite can improve substantially.
original_definitions.scope: All 46 Saturday UK/Irish races screened: maiden hurdle, active favourite or joint favourite a bumper winner with no previous hurdle start, and at least one rival with demonstrated relevant hurdle placing plus another supported hurdle route.
original_definitions.exclusions: Lastbutnotleased is a point recruit, not a recorded bumper winner; The Walk is already a hurdle winner; novice hurdle winners, chases, Flat novices and bumpers are outside v1.
original_definitions.counterargument: A festival bumper winner can have materially more potential than exposed hurdle opponents; the new trip can suit him.
original_definitions.limitations: One proposed case; race type and qualitative comparison restrict generalisation; no calibrated probability or profitable-edge claim.
original_definitions.weakening_evidence: Favourite’s jumping/ability comfortably surpasses named established rivals; beaten favourite owes defeat to an unanticipated newcomer rather than the proposed mechanism; adverse actual-price P/L or profits concentrated in few circumstances.
original_definitions.revision_policy: Any revision receives a new version before future races; earlier cases remain exploratory unless contemporaneously frozen under this version.

original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
Useful hurdle experience supplies opposition to a bumper winner making his hurdling debut. Soul Asylum has a hurdle run behind him; Jessbers Wish has actual placed hurdle form, rather than another speculative bumper transfer.

Winning case: Look Me won a bumper and was second in the Aintree Grade 2. That ability could transfer immediately and exceed the hurdle form on offer. His absence does not establish unfitness.

Decision: Keep the subsequent batch experimental: opponents have useful experience, but neither has demonstrated that it exceeds the favourite’s potential. At the short 3.00 Lay quote the second review still supports Watchlist only.

Ranked rivals:
1. Soul Asylum: Third at Wexford on hurdle debut, 10.75 lengths behind the winner, and entitled to progress. Finished 2.75 lengths behind Jessbers Wish while conceding 8 lb; they meet at equal 166 lb here. This is a comparative route, not a guaranteed reversal.
2. Jessbers Wish: Second in that Wexford hurdle, beaten 8 lengths, with an earlier hurdle fourth at Limerick. Loses his former 8 lb receipt from Soul Asylum; his Fairyhouse placing was a bumper, not a hurdle.
3. Young Rebel: Second in a Galway maiden hurdle and likely to benefit from a stronger test; still a maiden and must improve. Moonverrin is a serious further bumper-transfer possibility, not established hurdle opposition.

original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
A 9 lb higher mark and a move from Class 4 to Class 3 bring a recent chase debut winner against Rickety Bridge’s three demonstrated chase wins and Silver Hill’s actual chase experience.

Winning case: Torrent jumped well and won decisively on his first chase start. He can improve beyond the rise and still carries 7 lb less than Rickety Bridge. Earlier hurdle defeats do not prove a chase ceiling.

Decision: The rise is a condition of the experiment, not proof of vulnerability. Rickety Bridge has the clearest established chase route, but his latest jumping and 12.5-length defeat weaken the comparison. Watchlist, not an independent Pick.

Ranked rivals:
1. Rickety Bridge: Three chase wins at Newton Abbot over staying trips; a subsequent Plumpton third after a break. Raw full-result cumulative defeat was 12.5 lengths, not the 1.5-length adjacent-runner margin in the compact brief. Needs better jumping and to concede 7 lb.
2. Silver Hill: Fourth on chase debut, only 1.75 lengths behind the winner in a four-runner race; a more galloping test can suit. Only one chase start, so improvement remains a projection.
3. Champagne Chic: Useful staying hurdle winner, with a recent run behind him, but makes his chase debut. This is transferable hurdle ability, not another proven chase winner. Red Dirt Road and Solar System were also reviewed.

A strong hurdle mare meets an opponent with actual chase experience in Echoing Silence, plus useful alternative recruits. The competition is real; the favourite’s first chase start alone is not a fault.

Winning case: Her latest win was the Grade 1 mares hurdle at Punchestown, following a Fairyhouse second and Cheltenham third. She may simply have the highest ability and translate it to fences.

Decision: The hurdle class is substantial. Several rivals also need to transfer, so this remains a chase-transfer experiment at 4.00 rather than a Pick.

Ranked rivals:
1. Echoing Silence: Third, beaten 0.75 length, on Limerick chase debut, with a useful point/hurdle background. Can progress with that experience; one close third is not proof she is a better chaser.
2. Bambino Fever: Champion bumper winner with high potential; Cheltenham hurdle failure does not erase that ability. Also a chase debutant, so not independent established chase evidence.
3. Sainte Lucie: Two subsequent hurdle wins, including a Listed event; chasing physique supplies a route. Needs to transfer and has a 3 lb claim today. Mongibello’s actual chase second and Carrigmoornaspruce’s 7 lb claim are further relevant competition, fully retained in the field table.

original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
A recent chase winner returns to handicap company against Rockonliam’s two chase wins and Cheltenham second. Both leading horses are rated 132 and carry 161 lb after separate 5 lb claims, so the main contest is demonstrated chase ability rather than a manufactured weight edge.

Winning case: Karl has only gone up 2 lb, won after a previous chase second, and can improve again. His hurdle rating is not treated as a chase rating; his own 5 lb claim receives the same treatment as the rival’s.

Decision: Watchlist only at 5.00. The v1 operational scope requires a handicap chase today, latest completed race a chase win, a higher burden and comparable named chase evidence. His latest win was a novice, not a handicap; retain that boundary explicitly rather than rewriting the definition or calling him a serial handicap winner.

Ranked rivals:
1. Rockonliam: Won his first two chases, then second at Cheltenham, 1.5 lengths behind O’Moore Park. Today both he and Karl have 166 lb gross less 5 lb = 161 lb. He has risen too and is not receiving a unilateral claim advantage.
2. Watch The Weather: Recent chase third at Wexford, beaten 0.75 length; Listowel second was a hurdle, explicitly separate. His 158 lb less 3 lb = 155 lb may allow a challenge, but handicap terms broadly account for the rating difference.
3. El Champo: Runner-up in a Limerick handicap chase, with a useful 7 lb claim giving 146 lb. Less demanding opposition there and his own consistency limits the ranking. Kobalt St Georges is a reserve, so cannot count as continuing opposition without admission.

original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
The leading chase recruit faces actual graded chase experience: Lovely Hurling has three chase seconds; Frankie John has a Grade 3 chase win; Ocastle Des Mottes has two chase wins. These are established fence performances, unlike a list composed solely of alternative debutants.

Winning case: Zanoosh won five consecutive hurdles including a Grade 1, then ran second against males at Punchestown. Her 7 lb mares allowance gives 151 lb versus 158 lb for Lovely Hurling and 161 lb for penalised Frankie John. She may be a still better chaser.

Decision: The early-price second review at 3.35 supports Watchlist only. Stronger established chase opposition makes the experiment worthwhile, but the favourite’s own class and allowance are consequential. Do not call the drop to about 2m proven non-suitability.

Ranked rivals:
1. Lovely Hurling: Three chase seconds, including a 1.25-length Grade 3 defeat at Navan; 158 lb with no claim. Form is directly relevant but he returns after 267 days, which is uncertainty, not proof of unfitness.
2. Frankie John: Galway chase debut winner, then a Grade 3 winner and Cork second; 161 lb includes the 3 lb penalty. The 15-length latest defeat and shorter trip limit the route.
3. Ocastle Des Mottes: Two recent chase wins and track experience, 158 lb. Last win benefited from race position and requires further progress at this grade. Kainsbourg has shown useful chase ability too; Soir De Garde’s jumping/progress record is weaker.
